quickAnswer: In mainland China, call 110 for police, 120 for an ambulance, 119 for fire and 122 for traffic police. Give the exact location and describe what happened. If your phone cannot connect or you need language help, ask nearby staff to make the call. This website cannot dispatch emergency assistance.

sections.title: Mainland China emergency numbers
items: Numbers checked against the National Health Commission and UK government travel advice on October 22, 2026.
The links below can open a phone dialer when supported. You still need to place the call; opening this page does not contact a dispatcher.

sections.title: What to show locals

rows: Please help me call the police.
Please help me call an ambulance.
There is a fire. Please call 119.

items: Show the relevant phrase and the exact location to a nearby person who can help. Keep your hotel or destination name in Chinese available offline.

sections.title: Details to give when calling
items: Give the city, street address and a useful landmark; use the Chinese hotel or building name if you have it.
Describe the incident or symptoms plainly and answer the operator's questions.
If you cannot connect or communicate, ask nearby staff, hotel reception or another person with a working phone to help place the call.

sections.title: Hospital and passport reminders
items: For an urgent medical emergency, use 120 and follow the dispatcher's instructions. Ask local staff for help if needed.
For a lost or stolen passport, report the loss to local police or the Public Security Bureau, then contact your own embassy or consulate for replacement guidance.
If involved in a serious incident, contact your travel provider and insurer for assistance when immediate help has been arranged.

faqs.question: What are the emergency numbers in mainland China?
faqs.answer: Police 110, ambulance 120, fire 119 and traffic police 122. Give the exact location and describe the problem. Ask nearby staff for help if you cannot connect or communicate.

faqs.question: What should I do if I need a hospital in China?
faqs.answer: For an urgent medical emergency, call 120 or ask nearby staff to help place the call, then follow the dispatcher's instructions. This page provides reference numbers and phrases, not medical assessment.

faqs.question: What should I do if I lose my passport in China?
faqs.answer: Handle immediate safety needs, then report the loss to local police or the Public Security Bureau. Contact your own embassy or consulate for replacement instructions; keep any report they require.

faqs.question: Can ChinaEase Buddy contact emergency services for me?
faqs.answer: No. This website cannot dispatch help. A call link may open your device's dialer, but you or someone assisting you must place the call and speak with the service.
